questions.q: What is the first thing that happens when a user's question enters the retrieval step?
options: It is sent directly to the vector database as raw text
It is run through the same embedding model used on every stored chunk, producing a query vector
It is split into chunks using the same chunking strategy as ingestion
It is re-ranked before being embedded
questions.explain: The question text must be embedded with the same model used on every chunk so the resulting query vector is comparable in the same vector space.

questions.q: In a vector database search request, what does the 'limit' field control?
options: The maximum file size of the collection
The embedding model's dimensionality
The number of metadata fields returned per result
The number of closest-matching chunks to return — i.e., top_k
questions.explain: limit sets top_k — how many of the closest-matching stored vectors the search should return.

questions.q: What does the 'with_payload' field do in a vector database search request?
options: It filters results by metadata
It sets the similarity distance metric
It requests that each result include its stored text and metadata, not just an ID
It increases the number of results returned
questions.explain: with_payload: true tells the vector database to return the stored text and metadata alongside each matched vector's ID and score.

questions.q: What is the purpose of a metadata 'filter' passed alongside the query vector in a search request?
options: It restricts the search to points matching specific metadata, like a document ID or date range, before similarity is evaluated
It replaces the need for an embedding model
It re-ranks results after they are returned
It deletes points that don't match the filter
questions.explain: A filter scopes the similarity search to a subset of the collection — answering 'closest within this subset' rather than 'closest overall.'

questions.q: What does a high similarity score on a retrieved chunk actually guarantee?
options: That the chunk will automatically be cited in the final response
That the chunk is the most recently updated source in the collection
That the chunk's embedded meaning is close to the query's embedded meaning — not that it necessarily answers the question
That the chunk is factually correct
questions.explain: Retrieval only guarantees semantic closeness between the query and the chunk; whether the chunk actually answers the question, or is current and accurate, is judged later by re-ranking and the model itself.
